findings.quote: F₂ = 4 N is at 60° from oy, on the left side
findings.note: The served figure states F₂ is 60° above the −x direction and 30° from +y. The solution resolves a different vector from the one served.
findings.fix: F₂ = 4 N is at 60° above the −ox direction (30° from oy), so its ox-component is negative and its oy-component is positive.

findings.note: With the 60° measured from the leftward horizontal, the ox-component is −4cos60° = −2 N and the oy-component is 4sin60° = 2√3 N. The printed components are swapped.
Carries the swapped F₂ components into the collected result.
Wrong for the figure as served; the correct F₂ is (−2, 2√3) N ≈ (−2, 3.46) N.

findings.quote: Measuring F₂'s angle from ox instead of from oy, giving F₂ₓ = −4cos60° and F₂ᵧ = 4sin60° instead of the correct −4sin60° and 4cos60°.
findings.note: This condemns the correct resolution. For the served figure the 60° IS measured from the horizontal (−ox), so F₂ₓ = −4cos60° and F₂ᵧ = 4sin60° are right.
findings.fix: Measuring F₂'s 60° from oy instead of from the −ox direction, giving F₂ₓ = −4sin60° = −2√3 N and F₂ᵧ = 4cos60° = 2 N instead of the correct −2 N and 2√3 N.

notes: F₁, F₃, F₄ agree. The whole defect is one angle read from the wrong axis for F₂; the figure description is explicit and unambiguous about it.
